To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the current Web protocols are suboptimal and the gaps from the optimal grow with increasing link speeds, (ii) the main cause of the gap is the inherent dependencies between objects on Web pages, and (iii) a combination of a Mini CDN and Puppet running in a public cloud can significantly improve Web page load times.
(1) the current Web page loading protocol is suboptimal, and (2) the performance of the current Web page load protocol can be improved using a combination of a Mini CDN and a Puppet.
(1) the current multiplexing protocol, HTTP/1.x, is suboptimal, and (2) a combination of a content delivery network and a cloud based browser is a promising way to improve Web page load time.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of understanding and improving page load times on the modern web.
improving the performance of Web page loads on the modern network.
the design of a system that improves the performance of Web pages by moving the task of dependency resolution from the user's browser to a cloud.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the thesis is a good piece of work.

the thesis presents Mahimahi, a measurement toolkit that records websites and plays them back under emulated network environments, and Cumulus, a transparent proxy and headless browser that improves page loads by moving the task of dependency resolution from the browser to the proxy.
the thesis provides a novel and comprehensive measurement toolkit, MahiMahi, that records web sites and replays them in a network emulation environment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed an understanding of Web page load times, a tool for measuring them, and a system for accelerating them.

the thesis presents the first study that quantifies the impact of the Web's source level dependencies on page load performance, and presents the design of Cumulus, the first system that addresses this performance problem.
we developed Mahimahi, a tool that can be used to replay a website with a given network condition.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the performance of modern Web browsers is limited not by the network, but by the browser itself.
Web page load times can be significantly improved with simple, user deployable solutions, even without changing existing Web browsers or Web servers.
the Web's performance is limited by its architecture and the protocols that run over it.
